equation_request.abstract:
We discuss decoherence in discrete-time quantum walks in terms of a phenomenological model that distinguishes spin and spatial decoherence. We identify the dominating mechanisms that affect quantum walk experiments realized with neutral atoms walking in an optical lattice.

From the measured spatial distributions, we determine with good precision the amount of decoherence per step, which provides a quantitative indication of the quality of our quantum walks. In particular, we find that spin decoherence is the main mechanism responsible for the loss of coherence in our experiment. We also find that the sole observation of ballistic instead of diffusive expansion in position space is not a good indicator for the range of coherent delocalization.

We provide further physical insight by distinguishing the effects of short and long time spin dephasing mechanisms. We introduce the concept of coherence length in the discrete-time quantum walk, which quantifies the range of spatial coherences. Unexpectedly, we find that quasi-stationary dephasing does not modify the local properties of the quantum walk, but instead affects spatial coherences.

For a visual representation of decoherence phenomena in phase space, we have developed a formalism based on a discrete analogue of the Wigner function. We show that the effects of spin and spatial decoherence differ dramatically in momentum space.

specification.problem: Model a one-dimensional discrete-time (coined) quantum walk subject to per-step decoherence, with a phenomenological distinction between spin (coin) decoherence and spatial (position) decoherence, and extract the position distribution from which the decoherence per step can be inferred.
specification.reconstruction_scope: One smallest useful construction: a 1D coined quantum walk on a cyclic lattice of N=2^n sites (n=3, N=8) with a single coin qubit, a Hadamard coin, a conditional shift, and a phenomenological per-step channel composed of coin (spin) dephasing with probability p_s and position dephasing with probability p_x. Tiny instance: initial state |x=0>|up>, T=3 steps (no wrap-around), measure position. Outside scope: the atom-in-optical-lattice experimental mechanisms, the short-time versus long-time (quasi-stationary) spin-dephasing distinction, the coherence-length definition, the discrete Wigner-function formalism and momentum-space analysis, and all measured numerical values.

symbols.meaning: number of position qubits; lattice has N=2^n sites
lattice site index, encoded as the integer x mod N in the position register (binary, qubit 0 least significant)
coin operator acting on the coin qubit
density operator of the walker after t steps
probability of finding the walker at site x after t steps
Pauli Z on the coin qubit

equations.label: Coin operator (Hadamard coin)
equations.description: Balanced coin applied to the spin qubit before each shift.
equations.justification: The abstract does not specify the coin; the Hadamard coin is the simplest balanced choice for a minimal instance.
assumptions: Hadamard coin chosen; the experiment's actual coin (e.g. a microwave pi/2 pulse with some phase) may differ.

equations.label: Spin-dependent shift
equations.description: Moves the walker one site right if the coin is up and one site left if down; arithmetic is modulo N on the cyclic register.
equations.justification: Standard definition of the conditional shift in a discrete-time coined quantum walk; cyclic boundary is an encoding convenience.
assumptions: Cyclic lattice of N=2^n sites; for T < N/2 starting from x=0 no wrap-around occurs.

equations.label: Unitary walk step
equations.description: One coherent step of the discrete-time quantum walk.
equations.justification: Standard coined-walk step; the abstract names discrete-time quantum walks without giving this relation explicitly.

equations.label: Spin decoherence channel (per step)
equations.description: Phenomenological dephasing of the coin with probability p_s per step; it destroys coin coherences while leaving populations and position unchanged.
equations.abstract_quote: a phenomenological model that distinguishes spin and spatial decoherence
equations.justification: The abstract states a phenomenological per-step model separating spin decoherence; a coin dephasing channel is the simplest such model, but its exact form in the paper is not given in the abstract.
assumptions: Dephasing (not depolarizing or amplitude damping) form assumed; memoryless (Markovian) per-step application assumed, which does not capture the quasi-stationary dephasing discussed in the abstract.

equations.label: Spatial decoherence channel (per step)
equations.description: Phenomenological position dephasing with probability p_x per step; it destroys spatial coherences between different sites while preserving the position distribution.
equations.abstract_quote: a phenomenological model that distinguishes spin and spatial decoherence
equations.justification: The abstract introduces spatial decoherence as a distinct mechanism; position dephasing is the minimal model, but the paper's precise form is not available here.
assumptions: Pure position dephasing assumed; alternative spatial mechanisms (e.g. random site hopping) are not modelled.

equations.label: Full decoherent step and position distribution
equations.description: Iterated open-system map for the walk and the measured spatial distribution from which the decoherence per step is estimated.
equations.abstract_quote: From the measured spatial distributions, we determine with good precision the amount of decoherence per step
equations.justification: The abstract states that decoherence per step is extracted from measured spatial distributions, implying a per-step channel composed with the unitary step and a position-probability observable.
assumptions: Order of channels within a step (unitary, then spin, then spatial dephasing) is a choice; the two dephasing channels commute with each other but not with W.

equations.label: Ballistic versus diffusive spreading (background diagnostic)
equations.latex: \sigma^2(t) = \sum_x x^2 P(x,t) - \Big(\sum_x x P(x,t)\Big)^2, \qquad \sigma^2(t) \propto t^2 \ (\text{ballistic}),\quad \sigma^2(t) \propto t \ (\text{diffusive})
equations.description: Variance of the position distribution and its asymptotic scaling; the abstract warns this alone does not indicate the coherence range.
equations.justification: Standard characterization of quantum-walk spreading; included because the abstract discusses ballistic versus diffusive expansion. Scalings are asymptotic proportionalities, not exact equalities, and x is interpreted as a signed integer (sites x>N/2 mapped to x-N).
assumptions: Signed-integer reinterpretation of the modular position register is required for the variance to be meaningful.

registers.name: position
registers.role: Encodes the lattice site x mod 8 in binary (qubit 0 least significant); shift is increment/decrement mod 8 conditioned on the coin.

registers.name: coin
registers.role: Spin (internal) degree of freedom; |0> = up moves right, |1> = down moves left.

specification.initial_state: |x=0>_{position} ⊗ |up>_{coin} = |000>|0> (pure state, rho_0 = |psi_0><psi_0|). Assumption: localized start with a definite coin state.

steps.description: Prepare the position register in |000> and the coin in |0>.
Repeat for t = 1..T (T=3): apply the coin operator C to the coin qubit.
Apply the conditional shift S: controlled increment mod N on the position register if coin is |0>, controlled decrement mod N if coin is |1>.
Apply the phenomenological spin dephasing channel with probability p_s (e.g. by a classically randomized Z gate on the coin, or an ancilla-based Kraus implementation).
Apply the phenomenological spatial dephasing channel with probability p_x (e.g. randomized phase kicks diagonal in the position basis, or an ancilla-based implementation).
After T steps measure the position register in the computational basis to sample P(x,T).

specification.measurement: Computational-basis measurement of the n position qubits after T steps; repeated shots estimate P(x,T). The coin qubit may be traced out (not measured).
specification.classical_postprocessing: Reinterpret measured bitstrings as signed sites (x > N/2 -> x - N), build the histogram P(x,T), compute the variance per eq_7, and fit the simulated model (eq_6) with free parameters p_s and p_x to the measured distribution to estimate decoherence per step. The paper's specific fitting procedure is not available from the abstract.
assumptions: No experiment scope supplied; a minimal 1D coined walk on 8 cyclic sites with 3 steps was chosen as the instance.
Hadamard coin and localized initial state are choices, not taken from the abstract.

Spin and spatial decoherence are modelled as memoryless per-step dephasing channels; this is the simplest phenomenological model consistent with the abstract's description, not a verified reproduction of the paper's model.
Channel ordering within a step (W, then spin, then spatial dephasing) is a choice.
missing_information: Exact form of the paper's phenomenological spin and spatial decoherence model and its parametrization.
The actual coin operation and lattice/shift implementation used in the neutral-atom experiment.
Definition of the coherence length for the discrete-time quantum walk.
Model distinguishing short-time from long-time (quasi-stationary) spin dephasing and how it affects spatial coherences.
Definition of the discrete analogue of the Wigner function and the momentum-space analysis.
Measured decoherence-per-step values and the fitting procedure used to extract them.
